items.title: Security Council LIVE: Sudan’s war spreads as drones and hunger take a deadly toll
items.summary: As drone strikes kill civilians from El Obeid to Blue Nile and famine risk spreads across Darfur and Kordofan, the Security Council meets on Sudan – the world’s largest hunger and displacement crisis. Ambassadors are expected to press yet again for a ceasefire, safe aid access and an end to the weapons flows fuelling the brutal conflict.

items.title: ‘Hunger as a Weapon of War’ Threatens Millions, Third Committee Hears as Experts Warn of Crackdown on Youth Protests, Exclusion from Humanitarian Aid
items.summary: The deliberate use of hunger as a weapon of war, growing repression of youth-led protests and discrimination in humanitarian assistance are putting millions of people at risk, United Nations experts warned the Third Committee (Social, Humanitarian and Cultural) today, urging Governments to protect fundamental rights amid escalating conflicts and deepening global crises.

items.title: Myanmar Military Steps Up Airstrikes in Rakhine as Ground Offensive Stalls
items.summary: Crisis Group expert Thomas Kean examines why the Myanmar military’s faltering counteroffensive and escalating air attacks have further dimmed prospects for a ceasefire in Rakhine State.

items.title: IMF urges support for poorer nations facing high inflation, war spillovers
items.summary: Low-income countries spend up to 14 percent of their revenue on debt repayments, IMF chief says.

items.title: Ukraine: Critical health supplies destroyed in ongoing Russian attacks
items.summary: Ongoing and deadly Russian attacks across Ukraine are causing serious healthcare disruption, with more than $1.5 million-worth of medicines and supplies destroyed in four separate strikes on warehouses used by the UN there since July.

items.title: Fuelled by Relentless Fighting, Drone Attacks, Sudan’s Conflict, Plight of Its People Remains Bleak, Political and Peacebuilding Affairs Chief Warns Security Council
items.summary: The conflict and humanitarian crisis in Sudan continue to deteriorate without any visible breakthrough, Rosemary DiCarlo, Under-Secretary-General for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs, warned the Security Council today.

items.title: Toward a Thaw in the Cambodia-Thailand Border Conflict
items.summary: Hostilities between Cambodia and Thailand ceased in late 2025, after two rounds of combat along the frontier. But the truce is under growing strain. To avoid more war, the two countries should restore normal diplomatic ties and resume work on demarcating their shared border.

items.summary: Two vessels have been struck with naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz this week.

items.title: Gaza: 340 children killed despite ceasefire agreement - UNICEF
items.summary: A little over one year since a ceasefire agreement was announced between Hamas fighters and Israel, more than 340 children have been reported killed and hundreds more injured, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Friday.

items.summary: Defence Minister Guido Crosetto tells the BBC the US risks prolonging Russia's full-scale invasion rather than helping to end it.

items.title: Senior United Nations Official Warns Second Committee of Catastrophic Destruction in Gaza, Escalating Israeli Settlement Activity
items.summary: Escalating Israeli settler activity in the Palestinian territories and the Syrian Golan, along with the destruction of resources in Gaza represent an unprecedented catastrophe reversing “77 years of human development”, a senior United Nations official warned the Second Committee (Economic and Financial) today as it took up the issue of those lands.

items.title: Daily Press Briefing by the Office of the Spokesperson for the Secretary-General
items.summary: In Ukraine, large-scale attacks killed at least six civilians, injured 84 and disrupted power and water supplies across 11 regions. Attacks also damaged humanitarian facilities. The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission reported an 85 per cent rise in civilian casualties in September compared with a year earlier.

items.title: Security Council, 10245th Meeting (AM) Sudan
items.summary: At 10 a.m., the Security Council will hold a briefing on Sudan, held pursuant to resolution 2715 (2023), which requested the Secretary-General to provide a briefing every 120 days on the UN’s “efforts to support Sudan on its path towards peace and stability”. Under-Secretary-General for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs Rosemary DiCarlo is expected to brief.

items.title: Pulling Ethiopia and Eritrea Back from War
items.summary: Addis Ababa and Asmara are edging closer to a direct conflict, which would cause further mayhem in the troubled Horn of Africa and the Red Sea basin. It is not too late to avert disaster.

items.summary: Amid a rise in lethal Israeli strikes, demolitions and violence in Gaza and the West Bank, the Security Council held an open debate on Thursday focusing on the current situation in the Occupied Palestinian Territory.

items.title: Russian strikes kill civilians, injure dozens across Ukraine

items.title: Secretary Rubio’s Meeting with Dominican Republic Foreign Minister Bisonó Haza
items.summary: Office of the Spokesman Secretary Rubio’s Meeting with Dominican Republic Foreign Minister Bisonó Haza Readout October 16, 2026 Secretary of State Marco Rubio met today with Dominican Republic Foreign Minister Víctor Bisonó Haza in Washington to advance the strong U.S.–Dominican Republic partnership. The two discussed deepening security cooperation against the cartels and narco-terrorist groups that threaten our hemisphere. They also discussed continued collaboration under the U.S.–Dominican Republic Critical Minerals Framework to advance concrete investment in the mining sector.

items.title: Niger Wrestles with the Aftermath of a Military Revolt
items.summary: A mutiny by Niger’s special forces in late August morphed into a coup attempt. In this Q&A, Crisis Group experts explain how the unrest exposed growing discontent within the military’s ranks.

items.title: As disasters mount, next UN climate summit faces a test of trust
items.summary: Less than a month before the UN climate conference COP31 opens in Antalya, Türkiye, representatives of three successive summit presidencies gathered to address a pressing question: How can the world restore trust in climate action when the consequences of a warming planet are already being felt?

items.title: Could your brain data be used against you? UN calls for limits on neurotechnology
items.summary: Brain signals recorded by a gaming headset or a wellness gadget could one day be used as evidence against you in court, according to a new UN report which warns that neurotechnology is outpacing the laws meant to protect human rights.

items.title: The world is waging a ‘war on nature’ as progress on biodiversity targets lags
items.summary: Fewer than half of the national targets set to protect the world’s plants, animals and ecosystems are on track, the UN warns in a new report, days before countries gather in Yerevan, Armenia, for the COP17 biodiversity conference.

items.title: AI, green energy and economic transitions risk leaving vulnerable communities behind, UN warns
items.summary: Rapid transformations – from artificial intelligence and digital technologies to renewable energy and demographic shifts – are reshaping economies worldwide, creating new opportunities but also threatening to deepen socio-economic inequalities, a new UN report warned on Thursday.

items.title: Afghanistan faces record hunger levels amid rampant rights violations
items.summary: Acute malnutrition and hunger in Afghanistan have reached the highest levels ever recorded, with 15.9 million people facing acute food insecurity and conditions set to worsen in the coming months, according to a global hunger monitor report released on Thursday.

items.title: Trump waives several Russia sanctions as row with Zelensky intensifies
items.summary: The US president temporarily ends many restrictions on Moscow recently passed by Congress over "national security" concerns.

items.title: Navy Accepts Next-Generation Aircraft to Modernize Strategic Communications
items.summary: The Navy accepted a newly manufactured C-130J-30 Super Hercules aircraft from Lockheed Martin during a ceremony in Marietta, Georgia, marking the first step toward fielding the future E-130J Phoenix II.

items.title: Joint Interagency Task Force 401 Marks One Year of Accelerating Counter-UAS Capabilities
items.summary: The War Department marked its first year since establishing Joint Interagency Task Force 401, and has made rapid progress in delivering counter-unmanned aircraft systems capabilities to warfighters worldwide.

items.title: Hegseth Welcomes U.K. Counterpart to Pentagon
items.summary: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth hosted Wes Streeting, the United Kingdom's defense secretary, at the Pentagon, where the two leaders participated in a bilateral engagement.

items.title: Transparency, Confidence-Building Measures Take Centre Stage in First Committee Debate on Nuclear Weapons
items.summary: Transparency and confidence-building measures emerged as a central theme in the First Committee’s (Disarmament and International Security) first day of thematic debates on nuclear weapons, as States underscored their value in reducing nuclear risks amid ongoing arsenal modernization, the erosion of arms-control frameworks, and rising political tensions.
